original_question: Fix t>=3. Suppose F is a family of graphs on the vertex set [n] such that for every G,H in F, the intersection G intersect H has chromatic number at least t. Determine whether |F| <= 2^{C(n,2)-C(t,2)} must always hold.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.3 in 'Some problems on intersecting families of graphs' (David Ellis).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target essentially verbatim: it fixes t >= 3, considers a family F of graphs on the vertex set [n], assumes that for every G,H in F the intersection G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t, and asks whether the sharp bound |F| <= 2^{binom(n,2)-binom(t,2)} must hold. That is exactly the statement of Conjecture 4.3 in Section 4.
missing_details: Quantify n explicitly and state the intended range as integers n,t with 3 <= t <= n.
Specify that the objects are simple labelled graphs on the fixed vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n}; equivalently, F is a subset of the set of all edge-sets on [n].
Define G ∩ H as the graph on [n] with edge set E(G) ∩ E(H).
Clarify that the condition is for all G,H in F, including G = H, so each graph in F itself must have chromatic number at least t.
If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, introduce chromatic number notation explicitly, e.g. χ(G ∩ H) >= t.
To stay paper-faithful, keep the sharp exponent binom(t,2); do not weaken it to the separate weaker open problem Conjecture 4.4 with an unspecified absolute constant c > 0.

If desired for motivation, note that the bound matches the size of the obvious construction consisting of all graphs on [n] that contain a fixed copy of K_t, which is why Conjecture 4.3 is presented as a strengthening of Conjecture 4.1.
refined_question: For integers n,t with 3 <= t <= n, let F be a family of simple labelled graphs on the vertex set [n] = {1,2,...,n}. Assume that for every G,H in F, the graph G ∩ H on [n] with edge set E(G) ∩ E(H) satisfies χ(G ∩ H) >= t. Must it always be true that |F| <= 2^{binom(n,2)-binom(t,2)}?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 4, Conjecture 4.3, not a neighboring problem. The hypothesis and the claimed sharp upper bound coincide exactly with Conjecture 4.3. The surrounding context in Section 4 first defines H-intersecting families and the extremal function g_H(n), then states Conjecture 4.1 for K_t-intersecting families with the same extremal exponent, and immediately after says that Conjecture 4.3 is a strengthening of Conjecture 4.1. Proposition 4.2 records the weaker bound currently obtainable by an adaptation of the Chung-Frankl-Graham-Shearer argument, namely |F| <= 2^{binom(n,2)-t+1}, so the paper's intended sharp question is precisely the one in your draft rather than a broader variant. Conjecture 4.4 is a weaker relaxation with an unspecified absolute constant c > 0, so your draft should remain focused on the exact binom(t,2) exponent of Conjecture 4.3. The only reasons the draft is not fully complete are that it leaves n implicit, does not spell out that graphs are labelled/simple on the fixed vertex set [n], and does not explicitly define graph intersection as edge-set intersection.
